findings.title: HEAD d25362e breaks ProjectService.Create against its own migration 1010
findings.detail: Migration 1010_video_drop_script_column.up.sql drops video_project.script, and the commit message claims 'SELECT/Scan 同步收窄', but example/internal/video/app/service.go:345 INSERT...RETURNING still selects `script` — every Create fails on a freshly-migrated DB with SQLSTATE 42703 `column "script" does not exist`. Also the Scan list at :349-350 has 9 destinations for 10 RETURNING columns. Unit tests pass because they use fakes; the 3 DB integration tests (CreateMutateGet / OptimisticLockConflict / SubmitRender_GateOrder) are the only catch-net and they fail. This is a shipped, reproducible defect at HEAD — merge gate is RED.
findings.evidence: docker schema dump: video_project has no script column; go -C example test ./internal/video/app/ reproducible 3-test FAIL; git show HEAD:service.go line 345 unchanged

findings.title: Test stub cancelPipeline has an unsynchronized lazy-init data race → whole render package hangs
findings.detail: example/internal/video/render/worker_test.go:377-392: both waitStarted() and Run() do `if c.started == nil { c.started = make(chan struct{}) }` without any lock before the once.Do(close). When the test's goroutine (line 358-361) calls waitStarted() concurrently with the worker's Run(), both may allocate DIFFERENT channels; waitStarted blocks forever on the channel nobody closes, Work never returns, and the package dies at the test timeout. Reproduced: full-batch run hung 601.657s; isolated -run TestWorker -timeout 120s hung again; 8 bounded reruns = 2 hangs / 7 passes (25%). Real Chrome-using tests and stub pool tests share nothing here — §1.9's 'suspected cross-test interference' hypothesis is superseded: the race is INSIDE this one test's stub. Fix is mechanical (init channel in struct literal or guard with the existing once) — left to a code-change task, out of scope for this read-only audit.
findings.evidence: panic traces name worker_test.go:384 (waitStarted <-chan) both times; /tmp/render_all_8.txt

findings.title: cgo/-race unusable on this host: msys2 cc1.exe DLL deps point to deleted mingw64/bin
findings.detail: go test -race (any package importing runtime/cgo) and any `import "C"` build fail with silent `cgo.exe: exit status 2`. Root cause chain: gcc 15.2.0 (ucrt64) invokes cc1.exe; ldd shows cc1.exe resolves libgcc_s_seh-1/libgmp-10/libwinpthread-1/libzstd/zlib1 from /mingw64/bin — that directory does not exist (stale references from a removed mingw64 toolchain). gcc -c exits 1 with EMPTY stderr. Blocks V1/V2 race verification (§1.9 pending items) and any CGO_ENABLED=1 workflow. Repair hint: reinstall/repair msys2 mingw-w64 toolchain or purge the ghost mingw64 path from the install; retest with `gcc -c` on a trivial file before re-running race gates.
findings.evidence: ldd output for cc1.exe; minimal import-C probe fails identically with and without CC override

findings.title: Bootstrap-order dependency: TestRegisteredKeysFullLoop requires a pre-migrated DB
findings.detail: As anticipated by the task brief: TestRegisteredKeysFullLoop (cmd/app settings) does not self-bootstrap migrations. On a fresh DB it fails on missing site_settings; after video/app DB tests ran first (pgmigrate.Up + product chain), it PASSES (verified 0.14s green in this run). This is a test-design property, not a regression: any future CI using a fresh DB must run a self-bootstrapping package (e.g. ./internal/video/app/) or make -C example db-up before ./... sweeps, or the full-suite verdict will contain one spurious FAIL.
findings.evidence: --- PASS: TestRegisteredKeysFullLoop (0.14s) on bootstrapped DB in this run
